findings.summary: crates/server/src/sources.rs:51-53: the new repo naming only reaches the partial path. When no repo's PR list could be read (repos_read == 0), the read still bails with "no repo's PRs could be read, first: {first}" and ignores read.repos_failed. Say two repos are configured and both /pulls reads fail. last_error in the snapshot then names only the first repo, while the commit message says the source's error names every such repo. The per-repo tracing::warn at github.rs:122 does log both, so the blocking finding from Adversarial review round 4 (no log, repo unnamed behind a PR error) is fixed. Only this snapshot detail is left: putting read.repos_failed.join(", ") into the bail message would close it.
findings.reason: The bail message now names every failed repo.

findings.summary: crates/server/tests/github.rs:233-238: the new test checks only that last_error starts with "PR lists failed for bbooth/gone; ". Nothing checks the new per-repo tracing::warn (github.rs:122), the change the round-4 finding asked for. The log could be removed and every test would still pass. The test also reads sources[0], which is the github source only because this State has never refreshed any other source. Finding the source by name, as status() does a few lines earlier, would keep the test from breaking if another source is refreshed first. I couldn't run the tests because the scratchpad volume is out of disk space, so I didn't check whether this test passes.
findings.reason: Partly fixed: the test now finds the source by name and passes. The log line itself is still untested.
